# copick export cets

<span class="source-badge source-badge--core" title="Part of copick core">core</span>

*Export a project's tilt series, alignments and tomograms as a CETS dataset.*

## Usage

```bash
copick export cets [OPTIONS]
```

## Description

Writes one CETS (https://github.com/TomoBabel/cets-data-models) `Dataset` document: a `Region` per run with its
tilt series (per-image stage angle, acquisition order, dose and CTF), alignments (one `ProjectionAlignment` per
aligned image) and tomograms (with the tilt series they were reconstructed from), and the instruments and
acquisition sessions. Identifiers are prefixed with the run name. What CETS has no field for (copick's extensions,
alignment names and reference volumes, tomogram links) goes to a companion file next to it.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `-c, --config` | path | — | Path to the configuration file. |
| `--output, -o` | file | **required** | Path of the CETS JSON document to write. |
| `--run-names` | text | `""` | Comma-separated run names to export. Omit to export all runs. |
| `--tomograms / --no-tomograms` | boolean flag | `True` | Export the runs' tomograms (with their frames and the tilt series they were reconstructed from). |
| `--paths / --no-paths` | boolean flag | `True` | Record the URL of each tilt series and tomogram store. |
| `--validate / --no-validate` | boolean flag | `True` | Validate the document against the targeted CETS schema (needs jsonschema: pip install 'copick[cets]'). |
| `--companion / --no-companion` | boolean flag | `True` | Write <output>.copick-companion.json with the data CETS has no field for. |
| `--name` | text | — | Name of the dataset. Default: the project's name. |
| `--debug / --no-debug` | boolean flag | `False` | Enable debug logging. |

## Examples

```bash
# Export all runs
copick export cets -c config.json -o dataset.cets.json

# Export two runs without their tomograms
copick export cets -c config.json -o dataset.cets.json --run-names TS_001,TS_002 --no-tomograms
```
